extracted.intended_audience: members/readers of the Philosophical Transactions; natural philosophers and experimental scientists
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing short observational or experimental reports and instrument descriptions for publication in a learned natural-philosophy journal (e.g., Philosophical Transactions): include experiments, apparatus, observations, calculations, comparisons to prior work, and worked examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visible experimental demonstration; repeat and exhibit
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the phenomenon visibly (e.g., 'showed the circulation of the blood ... as plainly as water running in a river') and, when possible, repeat the experiment before the Society or audience so others can observe it ('I repeated again before them').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report conditions that make the phenomenon visible (transparency of skin/vessels, observing eyes), note how long specimens lived after preparation (e.g., 'I have had them live 8 hours after they have been expanded, and all their viscera laid open'), and give direct descriptive comparisons (like 'as plainly as water running in a river') to convey what observers should see.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed apparatus construction and parts (including valves, pipes, seals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the physical construction of devices in detail: names/positions of parts, how they connect (pipes, valves, soldering, luted joints), and any concealed or secret placements (e.g., 'a pipe concealed in the coral ... well soldered', 'the outer glass or case being close luted at the head').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give exact functional descriptions of components (e.g., which valve prevents backflow), specify materials/joins (soldered, luted), and explain why each part is necessary for the device's operation. Where secrecy or hidden parts are relevant to performance, note their placement and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide figures/plates and label references
rubrics_metrics.description: Include and reference diagrams/plates/figures (e.g., 'fig. 5, pi. 5', 'pi. 8, fig. 2') to accompany descriptions of instruments, anatomy, and mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure labels in text match plate/figure labels and refer readers to particular parts of the image when describing construction or anatomy; use the figures to show proportions and spatial relations that are cumbersome in prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stepwise operational procedures and numbered instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Give explicit step-by-step methods for using instruments and for performing calculations (e.g., Flamsteed's 1–6 steps to find satellite distances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number the steps, state required inputs (parallax, eclipse times), and indicate the sequence of operations; include any decision points (e.g., when to add or subtract parallax) so a reader can reproduce the procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include worked examples applying the method to real dates/data
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the method by applying it to real cases with full calculations (e.g., worked examples for Dec 26, 1685 and July 16, 1686 showing numerical steps and resulting semidiameters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the raw data used, intermediate results (parallactic intervals, half-durations, last immersions), and final interpreted outcomes; worked examples clarify conventions (signs, units, augmentations) and aid reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record precise observational times and phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Give exact times for events and phases of observations (e.g., times for penumbra, beginning of eclipse, total immersion, emersion: 'At 9h 32m 25s the penumbra', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record times with as much precision as practical, and note any observational difficulty that affects precision (dense penumbra, clouds). When giving phases, specify how times were obtained and any corrections applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe observational technique, required skill, and difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how observations were made and the practical difficulties encountered (e.g., 'required no small skill and labour to manage our tubes... to keep them sufficiently steady', dealing with clouds and severe season).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report instrument lengths, mounting/steadying methods, environmental conditions, and techniques to distinguish features (penumbra vs. true eclipse), so others understand the skill and setup needed to replicate observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative physical reasoning and computation to test claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Use physical principles and numerical computation to assess claims (e.g., refutation of a perpetual-motion contrivance by computing atmospheric pressure equivalents: mercury columns of 22 vs 29 inches giving only 7 inches effective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the numerical comparisons and physical argument explicitly (how much atmospheric pressure is counterpoised by mercury, what that implies for net forces), so theoretical impossibilities or shortcomings are demonstrated logically and quantitatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: State approximations, assumed values, and when extra accuracy is unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare assumed standard approximations and indicate when greater exactness is needless (e.g., assume half-duration for first satellites 'ih. 10m.' and 'greater exactness being needless').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state approximations used, justify them (practical insignificance or tabular availability), and advise when more exact measures would or would not materially change the results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for sign/convention choices affecting results (e.g., parallax additive/subductive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly note conventions that change outcomes (e.g., whether parallax is to be added or subducted, which side of Jupiter the shadow lies on if parallax is additive/subductive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the rule for sign/convention explicit, show how it affects the computations and the final positional interpretation (right/left), and illustrate with examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare findings to prior observations and authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Situate new measurements and assertions in the context of earlier observations and authors (e.g., compare computed earth-degree/miles with Norwood and Picart; compare magnetic declination with earlier value 'just 5° 5' to the west').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite previous results, note agreement or small differences, and discuss possible reasons (measurement inaccuracy, stationarity vs gradual change). This helps validate results or indicate anomalies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give measurements, units, and conversions explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: State dimensions, units, and conversions when deducing derived quantities (e.g., English foot divided into 1000 parts, conversion factors between various ancient feet and miles resulting in a degree = 72½ English miles of 5000 feet each).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the arithmetic and the chain of conversions used to derive large-scale quantities so readers can follow and verify; indicate the sources or monuments measured when deriving ancient units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide anatomical descriptions with precise location, size and connections
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting anatomical observations, give exact seat/location, shape variability, size/weight estimates, vascular/nerve supply, ducts and openings (e.g., a new gland 'seated in the orbit of the eye... size of a small nut... has 4 sorts of vessels... artery from the carotid').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the organ's relations to neighboring structures, give measurements, note variability, and, where possible, provide comparative instances across species and figures to support identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize statistical counts or tabular data when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where aggregate counts are relevant, present them succinctly (e.g., 'Christened. Males 7484 Females 7246 In all 14730; Buried. Males 11891 Females 11331 In all 23222').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide totals and sensible breakdowns (sex, age, date span), and include such tables or summaries to give readers immediate sense of scale and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report limitations, uncertainty, and cautious assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly acknowledge uncertainty and limits of one’s data or assertions (e.g., 'I am not willing to assert that...', 'this doubt has probably been owing to some inaccuracy in the observations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State where data are insufficient, when conclusions are tentative, and identify likely sources of error (observational inaccuracy, seasonal effects) so readers can weigh the claims appropriately.
